رِئَآءٌ an inf. n. of 3 [q. v.]. (M. [Said in the S to be a subst.]) ―
-b2- [Hence,] قَوْمٌ رِئَآءٌ A party, or company of men, facing one another. (S.) And in like manner, بُيُوتُهُمْ رِئَآءٌ [Their tents, or houses, are facing one another]. (S.) And مَنَازِلُهُمْ رِئَآءٌ Their places of alighting, or abode, are facing, or opposite, one to another. (T.) ―
-b3- And دُورُ القَوْمِ مِنَّا رِئَآؤٌ The houses of the people, or party, are as far as the eye reaches, where we see them, namely, the people. (M.) ―
-b4- And هُمْ رِئَآءُ أَلْفٍ They are as many as a thousand in the sight of the eye. (K, * TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
